For 12-year-old Jennifer Odom’s murder, jury says man should die

The panel deliberated 2 1/2 hours before unanimously recommending the death penalty for Jeffrey Norman Crum Sr.
 
 
1
 
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:08
Instaread
By
  • Dan SullivanTimes staff
Published Yesterday|Updated Yesterday
Advertisement

The 1993 murder of 12-year-old Jennifer Odom was so heinous and cruel that Jeffrey Norman Crum Sr. should forfeit his life for it, a Hernando County jury decided Tuesday.

The same panel of seven men and five women that last week found Crum guilty of the notorious crime unanimously recommended that he be sentenced to death.

Their decision took 2½ hours. It came on what would have been Jennifer’s 46th birthday.

    1. Comment by K. Newman.

      10 hrs ago

      Based on the track record of recent executions, the normal course of the legal proceedings in death penalty cases seems to take at least 30 years to play out. This is more a symbolic sentence than a practical one, but the jury is saying unequivocally that he deserves the maximum sentence allowable in Florida. If this was NJ, that would be 15-20.
